competitors.title: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md & Copilot Instructions: Configure Every AI Coding Assistant
key_points: Complete landscape of 9 AI config file formats: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, .cursorrules, .cursor/rules/*.mdc, copilot-instructions.md, .github/instructions/*.instructions.md, .windsurfrules, .windsurf/rules/*.md
AGENTS.md is the closest universal standard, stewarded by Linux Foundation with 60,000+ open-source projects
Codex CLI supports AGENTS.override.md for local-only overrides (gitignored) — committing this file is a security anti-pattern
CLAUDE.md has 5-layer hierarchy: global (~/.claude/) → workspace → project root → subdirectory → path-scoped rules
GitHub Copilot scoped instructions with glob-pattern frontmatter since July 2025 — can override per-file-type behavior
CLAUDE.md reads AGENTS.md as fallback, enabling cross-tool compatibility but expanding the trust boundary
Codex CLI size limit: project_doc_max_bytes (default 64 KiB, older versions 32 KiB) — content past the cap is silently truncated
Recommended approach: AGENTS.md as single source of truth, tool-specific files only for unique features

competitors.title: AI Coding Assistant Config Files Compared: CLAUDE.md vs .cursorrules vs copilot-instructions.md
key_points: Comparison matrix: hierarchy depth, global config, token visibility, format, memory/learning, cross-platform support across 5 formats
Highlights config fragmentation problem: 5 projects × 3 tools = 15 config files to maintain
CLAUDE.md has the most sophisticated hierarchy (5 layers) and only format with token visibility and persistent memory
AGENTS.md is closest to universal standard; supported by Codex CLI, Cursor, Claude Code (fallback), Continue.dev, Aider
No tool has built-in config validation, integrity checking, or security scanning for agent config files
TokenCentric dashboard provides real-time token counting, Monaco editor, hierarchy visualization — but no security scanning

competitors.title: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md: The Configuration Layer That Makes AI Coding Agents Actually Follow Your Rules
key_points: Instruction budget problem: frontier LLMs follow ~150-200 instructions; Claude Code system prompt uses ~50 slots
CLAUDE.md features: @import syntax, path-scoped rules with YAML frontmatter, 5-level hierarchy, auto-memory, hooks
Auto-memory writes session notes to ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ — creating an organic learning layer but also a sensitive data exposure risk
Hooks in .claude/settings.json are deterministic (always enforced); CLAUDE.md instructions are advisory (model decides relevance)
AGENTS.md open standard supported by 60+ tools; maintained by Agentic AI Foundation under Linux Foundation
Key security insight: 'use a linter instead of instructions for code style — never send an LLM to do a linter's job'
OpenAI Codex repo uses 88 AGENTS.md files across monorepo — large surface area for config manipulation
Windsurf has dual-layer model: explicit .windsurf/rules/ (version-controlled) + Cascade Memories (local-only)

competitors.title: CLAUDE.md vs AGENTS.md vs MEMORY.md vs SKILLS.md vs CONTEXT.md: The Ultimate AI File Hierarchy Guide for 2026
key_points: Over 70% of developers using AI coding assistants unaware of instruction file differences — leading to duplication, token waste, and confused agents
Five-file hierarchy: CLAUDE.md (identity), AGENTS.md (architecture), MEMORY.md (persistent log), SKILLS.md (task-specific), CONTEXT.md (session state)
MEMORY.md transforms agents from stateless tools to collaborative partners — but also accumulates sensitive architectural decisions and past mistakes
SKILLS.md dynamic loading saves context window tokens but means config files may load unexpectedly based on task detection
CONTEXT.md captures 'tribal knowledge' — undocumented quirks and gotchas — which may include security-sensitive information
Key insight: auto-memory mechanism means agent instruction files grow over time, creating a larger attack surface for injection

competitors.title: CLAUDE.md vs .cursorrules vs AGENTS.md: Three-Way Comparison
key_points: Cursor .cursorrules now deprecated in favor of .cursor/rules/*.mdc with 4 activation modes: Always Active, Auto Attached (glob-matched), Agent Requested, Manual
Always Active rules affect every single session — highest security impact if manipulated
Auto Attached rules activate based on file patterns — attacker could target high-value file types
AGENTS.md closest to universal standard; AGENTS.override.md provides gitignored local-only overrides
Next.js (138K stars), n8n (178K stars) among major projects using AGENTS.md
Format migration: Cursor rules moved from single file to directory-based system for better scope control

angles: The invisible attack surface: every AI config file in your repo is an instruction injection vector — how to audit and harden CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursor/rules, and copilot-instructions.md
Git trust boundaries: committed config files are part of the repo trust chain — how malicious PRs can inject instructions that override agent safety constraints
The hierarchy blind spot: CLAUDE.md has 5 layers from ~/.claude/global to subdirectory files — an attacker who compromises any layer controls agent behavior in that scope
AGENTS.override.md and local-only files: the gitignored files that should stay gitignored — and how committing them creates a persistent backdoor
Secret management in agent configs: why env vars, API keys, and internal architecture details don't belong in config files that agents read at session start
Token budget as security constraint: with only ~100-150 instruction slots available, security rules compete with productivity rules — how to prioritize both
The auto-memory risk: Claude Code's session notes (MEMORY.md pattern) accumulate sensitive project decisions, configurations, and past mistakes — treat as a sensitive document
Multi-tool fragmentation: teams using CLAUDE.md + .cursorrules + copilot-instructions.md have three separate trust boundaries to maintain and audit
From advisory to deterministic: how to use hooks (.claude/settings.json) and linters for security rules that cannot be overridden by instruction injection
OWASP agent security applied: mapping config file vulnerabilities to OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications — goal hijacking (ASI01), privilege escalation, and data exposure
